name: Make good espresso
blurb: Espresso is a variables problem: dose, grind, time and yield. Once you learn to change one thing at a time and taste the result, you can dial in any coffee.
gear: An espresso machine and a decent burr grinder — the grinder matters more
A tamper and a distribution tool
Fresh beans, roasted within a month
steps: Fix your dose by weight for your basket — typically 18 g for a double — and keep it constant while you learn.
Distribute the grounds evenly, then tamp level with consistent pressure. Level matters more than force.
Pull a shot and record grind setting, dose, yield and time. A common starting target is 36 g out in 25 to 30 seconds.
Taste it. Sour and thin means under-extracted, so grind finer. Bitter and harsh means over-extracted, so grind coarser.
Change one variable at a time and re-taste. This is the entire discipline.
Learn to steam milk to a glossy microfoam once the espresso itself is good.
tips: The grinder is the limiting factor. A great machine with a bad grinder makes bad espresso.
Beans need a few days off roast and go stale after a month. Freshness is a variable too.
Channelling — water finding a fast route through the puck — shows as spraying or a fast, thin shot. Fix the distribution.
proof: Three consecutive shots within a second and a gram of your target, all tasting balanced.
